editorial.evidence: Re-review against all 46 captured sections. The previous version had 46 one-per-section rows with shared boilerplate evidence and had thinned or dropped: the Acme CEO trace (main-intro), the functional list, the non-functional target table and interview shortcut, the opening-move timing and 'is that the system?' quote, context rot and lost-in-the-middle, 'stop too early vs never stop', the outcome-vs-trajectory six-wasted-hops example, the what-to-test list, two of the supervisor build's four costs, the platform's four delta pieces, both two-minute answers, the eight carrying lines, the 60-second close, the four cost verbs, the references' supported claims, and 9 of 14 takeaways; it also reworded several check-yourself questions, rendered the 45-minute table's last cell as ', ', left the cost card with empty headers, and captioned every figure 'source figure N'. Rewrote into a 12-step walkthrough mirroring the full design's order, 9 deep dives (trust, evidence records, cost, grader, supervisor build, platform, three variants, references), 9 practice groups with 25 reveals, and 4 Quick review groups, giving 117 item-level rows. Defined terms before use (agent, sub-agent, ledger, reducer, last-write-wins, oracle, Little's Law, prefix caching, trifecta, exfiltration, control plane, trust zones, grade distribution), added worked examples (Acme trace, three-branch loss, $0.80 per-branch budget, image-URL exfiltration, 117→120 arithmetic, 10/15/20-second parallel latency), recast the source author's first-person 'my own build' as attributed, and labelled additions (reserve-then-reconcile budget, follow-up applications, two changed-constraint drills). Source inconsistencies resolved in text (2026-11-16): section 4 figure lead-ins one figure off → each figure introduced by what its SVG draws, meta note removed; 'after 12 hops' discovery question vs eight-hop cap and 3-12-step plan → question set to eight hops (the cap the termination code enforces), steps and hops stated as separate counters; 'roughly $0.20' vs '$0.20 ceiling' → ceiling throughout, because the budget dict, failure ladder and state table all enforce it as a per-run stop (whether the business treats it as hard stays a discovery question); 'this enterprise case' vs consumer product → consumer product that holds private documents, so it still needs per-user ACLs and a release gate. The summary paragraph listing these in the references section is removed.
